core_obligations: Show that a proper top dimensional component gives nonvanishing H^d via a dualizing module, proving (1) implies (3) (proof lines 9394-9404).
Show (3) implies (1) by filtering a coherent F with nonvanishing H^d, passing to an integral subscheme with an ideal sheaf and applying the Lichtenbaum lemma (proof lines 9406-9426).
Prove (1) and (2) equivalent by writing a quasi-coherent module as a filtered colimit of coherent submodules (proof lines 9428-9438).
proof_roadmap: (1) implies (3) via a dualizing module (proof lines 9394-9404).
Equivalence of (1) and (2) via filtered colimits (proof lines 9428-9438).
difficulty_reason: For a nonempty separated scheme X of finite type over a field k with d = dim(X), the theorem shows the equivalence of three conditions: H^d(X, F) = 0 for all coherent F, the same for all quasi-coherent F, and no irreducible component of dimension d being proper over k (statement lines 9380-9392). For (1) implies (3) the proof takes an irreducible component X' which is proper of dimension d, uses a dualizing module omega_{X'} of X' over k from Lemma labelled lemma-duality-proper-over-field for which H^d(X', omega_{X'}) is nonzero because it is dual to H^0(X', O_{X'}), and concludes that H^d(X, omega_{X'}) is nonzero (proof lines 9394-9404). For (3) implies (1) it takes a coherent F with H^d(X, F) nonzero and a filtration 0 = F_0 subset ... subset F_m = F as in Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-coherent-filter, so that some quotient F_{i+1}/F_i has nonzero H^d; this produces an integral closed subscheme Z and a nonzero coherent ideal sheaf I on Z with H^d(Z, I) nonzero, and Lemma labelled lemma-lichtenbaum then gives dim(Z) = d with Z proper over k, contradicting (3) (proof lines 9406-9426). Finally (1) and (2) are shown equivalent for any Noetherian X: one direction is trivial, and for the other every quasi-coherent F is the filtered colimit of its coherent submodules by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-quasi-coherent-colimit-finite-type, so H^d vanishes by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit (proof lines 9428-9438). Reducing the coherent case to a single integral subscheme with an ideal sheaf, and the quasi-coherent case to a filtered colimit, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the author notes in the surrounding text that the most interesting part of the argument sits in the proof of the preceding lemma, which this lane counted separately.
